To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have cloned and characterized the cDNAs of the BamHI-H family of mRNAs that are strongly associated with tumorigenesis in Marek's disease.
we have cloned and characterized four cDNAs that are associated with the tumorgenicity of MDV.
the cDNAs from tumorigenic strains encode proteins that are similar to oncogenes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterization of the BamHI-H family of RNAs associated with Marek's disease (MD) tumor induction by MDV.
identifying the genes that are responsible for the tumorigenic properties of the virus.
the isolation and characterization of BamHI-H gene transcripts that are associated with the tumorgenicity of MDV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cDNAs isolated in this study represent the first characterization of the BamHI-H RNAs that are associated with the tumourigenic potential of MDV.
the BamHI-H RNAs are associated with tumorigenity and are derived from a complex set of transcripts that may be spliced and/or nonspliced.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 132-bps repeats are associated with the tumorgenic potential of MDV.
the 132-bpbamHI-H gene family is composed of at least five distinct genes, each of which may play an important role in the pathogenesis of Marek'sdisease.
the cDNAs from RNAs of the BamHI-H family of MDV are associated with tumorigenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cDNAs we have isolated from tumorigenic MDV are not related to any known viral or cellular oncogene.
these BamHI-H gene products may be important in MDV-induced tumorigenesis.
the cDNA clones that we have isolated from the BamHI-D/H region of MDV DNA are derived from RNAs associated with virus-induced tumorigenesis and may encode proteins that are involved in this process.
